conviction_note: Near non-result: no company-level number the market has not seen. The evidence is a Tennessee peer's 12bp NIM compression on funding costs (FBK, 10-13), a Fed hike on 09-16 that barely touches Q3, guided Q3 payoffs, a consensus ($0.63) that sits below Q2's adjusted $0.64, and short interest that built ~17% into mid-September with the stock down 5.2% over 20 days. Those offset, so p_up is 52 on an abs move of 2.8 (median 2.14 plus some room for NIM and rate commentary under a new hiking cycle). The findings sum to -0.1 and the scaled number to +0.11. Both are effectively zero and differ only by rounding.

findings.finding: FB Financial (FBK), a Nashville-based Tennessee peer that overlaps the Knoxville footprint HOMB bought with Mountain Commerce, reported Q3 2026 on 2026-10-13. NIM fell to 3.83% from 3.95%, cost of interest-bearing deposits rose to 2.88% from 2.81%, and EPS was $1.21 adjusted against roughly $1.19-1.21 consensus. HOMB's own interest-bearing deposit cost was already rising in Q2 (2.39% from 2.35%) while loan yield fell (7.00% from 7.08%) and NIM held flat at 4.51% only with MCBI accretion. The bar ($0.63 against Q2's $0.64) implies roughly flat NII.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: HOMB's NIM has been its defining line. Q2 2026 (flat 4.51% NIM, record revenue, beat) bought +4.78%. Q3 2025 fell -3.39% despite an EPS beat ($0.61 vs $0.60). Q1 2026 fell -3.36% (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: FBK reported the evening before, and HOMB's consensus ($0.63) predates it. If the market had marked HOMB's NIM down on the read-through, consensus or price targets would have moved this week. None did, and the latest targets date from August-September.
findings.independence: Regions' Aug-Sep 2026 investor deck guided Q3 NIM stable to modestly higher and deposit costs roughly stable if rates were unchanged, which cuts the other way (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001281761/000128176126000057/a3q26investormeetingmate.htm). This is a peer proxy, not a company number.

findings.finding: The FOMC raised the funds rate 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, its first hike since July 2023, by a 12-0 vote. The minutes (released 10-07) show most officials expect another hike by year-end. This is HOMB's first print, and first outlook commentary, inside a hiking cycle. For Q3 itself the effect is about two weeks. The sign for HOMB is unclear: a 7.00% loan yield with a large floating book argues asset-sensitive, while rising deposit pricing (see FBK) argues the other way. HOMB has not disclosed its current rate sensitivity in anything I could read.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior HOMB print was inside a hiking cycle within the baseline's 7 events.
findings.why_not_priced: The hike itself is public and priced. What is unpriced is HOMB's own read of what it does to NIM, which comes on the 10-15 call. If the market had a view, HOMB's 20-day -5.2% would track a sector-wide move; I could not establish that it does.
findings.independence: This is macro-to-company transmission that the company has not confirmed. The FBK finding is the only direct read, and it is a different document.

findings.finding: On the Q1 2026 call, management guided up to $1B of loan payoffs in each of Q2 and Q3, against a normal run-rate just under $200M. In Q2, legacy loans instead grew about $26M (community banking +$46.4M, Centennial CFG -$22.6M) against an internal forecast of a ~$600M decline, so some of the guided payoffs may have slipped into Q3. Organic loan contraction in Q3 is therefore guided, not a surprise.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Loan balances beat the payoff guide in Q2, and the stock rose +4.78% on that print.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. It is company guidance, and the $0.63 bar sits below Q2's $0.64, which is consistent with analysts modelling payoffs. If payoffs come in well under $1B again, as in Q2, that is upside the bar does not hold.
findings.independence: Q2 release balance data (https://finviz.com/news/368831/record-revenue-and-successful-mountain-commerce-bancorp-acquisition-drive-strong-second-quarter-results-for-homb). The guidance itself comes from a third-party call summary, not the transcript.

findings.finding: The arithmetic of the bar is mildly favourable. Q2's $0.64 adjusted included $3.6M of purchase accretion plus $1.7M of event interest income (about $0.02/share after tax on ~200M shares), so core Q2 was about $0.62. Q3 adds a 92nd day of NII (about $0.01), and HOMB bought back 1.5M shares at $26.94 in Q2 with the stock below $30 for most of Q3. Consensus of $0.63 therefore sits about at the core run-rate, and HOMB beat in each of the last two quarters ($0.64 vs $0.61; $0.61 vs $0.60 in Q3 2025).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Beats were mixed: Q2 2026 beat +4.78%; Q3 2025 beat -3.39%; 5 of 7 prints rose (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced, since every analyst has the same release. The only unmodelled part is Q3 buyback volume, which no filing since the 10-Q discloses.
findings.independence: Two agreeing consensus sources: https://www.benzinga.com/quote/HOMB/earnings-forecasts and https://www.alphaquery.com/stock/HOMB/earnings-history. Shares the Q2 release with the payoff finding.

findings.finding: Short interest rose 1.42M shares (+17%) into the 2026-09-15 settlement to 9.95M (7.15 days to cover) and held at 9.91M (5.98 DTC) on 09-30. Meanwhile the stock slid from $30.86 (08-11) to $28.19, 5.2% down over 20 days. An in-line print from a name with ~6 days to cover and a sell-side average target near $33 gives shorts a reason to cover.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None measurable. Short interest at ~5% of shares has not visibly driven past reactions.
findings.why_not_priced: The build is public FINRA data, but the 20-day drawdown has no company cause I could find, so part of the de-rating looks like positioning rather than information. If shorts had already covered, the 09-30 settlement would show it falling.
findings.independence: Hovde initiated Outperform at $34 on 2026-09-08 and Stephens rates it Buy at $35 (https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/HOMB/forecast/).

findings.why_not_priced: It is public and small; the stock has since fallen 8.6%, so whatever signal it carried is in the price.

findings.finding: HOMB raised its quarterly dividend to $0.23 from $0.21 on 2026-07-22 and paid it 09-02. The raise is public and capital-return intent is unchanged; the only question for the print is whether Q3 buybacks continued at Q2's pace (1.5M shares).
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced. It is filed so the judges see the capital-return posture.

lessons_applied: Rule 6 (inside the guided range): the payoff finding moved from -0.2 to -0.1, because the company guided Q3 payoffs itself.
Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the beat-arithmetic finding moved from +0.3 to +0.2, because HOMB sold a beat in Q3 2025 (-3.39%).
Rule 7: short interest was checked before the negatives. It is about 5% of shares and 6 days to cover, moderate rather than crowded, so the FBK negative stays at -0.4.
Rule 5: the FBK and Fed findings stay filed as small proxies. The two edits offset, so impact_sum is unchanged at -0.1.
